_note: Help text for validation rule topics and general topics (spec 7C.5, 7B.11).

topics.title: Allowed ranges
topics.body: Every setting has a lowest and highest value, taken from the Bluetooth or Wi-Fi specifications or from this tool's data. A value outside it cannot be simulated.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Required values
topics.body: Every setting needs a number or a choice. An empty box has no meaning, so it has to be filled in.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Scan window and interval
topics.body: The scan window is how long a device listens in each scan interval, so it cannot be longer than the interval.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Packet length
topics.body: Each packet type has a fixed length in slots. It has to fit inside the time its link reserves.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Simulation window
topics.body: The window is the stretch of time that is simulated. It must be long enough to show several repeats of the slowest task.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Bluetooth Core versions
topics.body: Newer features need a newer Bluetooth Core version. The device version is a platform setting.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Wi-Fi generations, bands and widths
topics.body: Each Wi-Fi generation supports certain bands and channel widths. Wi-Fi 7 can use 320 MHz only in the 6 GHz band, for example.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: LE PHYs and LE Audio
topics.body: The 2M and Coded PHYs and isochronous audio were added in later Core versions.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Wi-Fi features
topics.body: Some tasks need a feature, such as target wake time or multi-link operation, that only newer generations have.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Frequency overlap
topics.body: Only 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi overlaps Bluetooth in frequency. At 5 and 6 GHz the two interact only through the shared antenna, core and isolation.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Wi-Fi roles
topics.body: A device acts as a station or as an access point. Doing both at once needs multi-role support.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Reserved voice slots
topics.body: Voice links reserve slots on a fixed pattern. Two links may not claim the same slots.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Tasks that exclude each other
topics.body: Some activities cannot run at once. A device cannot be scanning and initiating a connection on the same radio window, for example.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Device limits
topics.body: A device supports only so many simultaneous links of each kind. The limits are platform settings.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Audio and voice together
topics.body: Streaming audio and a voice call at once is legal but the voice link takes priority.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Duplicate tasks
topics.body: Two copies of the same task are allowed, but this is often a mistake.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Readability
topics.body: With many tasks the diagram becomes hard to read. The tool still runs but shows density bars when zoomed out.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: One radio, one channel
topics.body: One Wi-Fi radio can be on one channel at a time. Tasks on different channels cannot be simultaneous unless the device has more radios or links.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Slot budget
topics.body: Bluetooth Classic has a fixed number of slots. Reserved links and periodic tasks use them, and what is left is for data.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Airtime
topics.body: A technology cannot transmit for more than 100 percent of the time. If the tasks ask for more, the stream cannot be carried.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Cores serving tasks
topics.body: Each core can serve one radio at a time. With too few cores some tasks can never run together.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Platform consistency
topics.body: The front-end arrangement and the antenna mode must agree. Shared switch means one antenna; separate means two.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Isolation range
topics.body: Isolation is measured in decibels. Values outside 0 to 100 are not physical for this model.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Concurrency with low isolation
topics.body: Running both radios at the same time with little isolation lets the transmitter deafen the receiver.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Adaptive hopping settings
topics.body: Adaptive hopping removes channels under Wi-Fi. It has no effect without Wi-Fi in 2.4 GHz, and it cannot leave fewer than the minimum number of channels.
topics.label: STANDARD

topics.title: Time-share settings
topics.body: The Bluetooth share must be between 0 and 100 percent and the slice long enough to hold a useful block.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Performance
topics.body: Very many blocks make the diagram slow. The tool switches to density bars, and you can shorten the window.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

topics.title: Conflicts
topics.body: A conflict is a moment when a Bluetooth block and a Wi-Fi block overlap in time and also interact: their frequencies overlap, they share an antenna or core, or isolation is below the threshold. The severity says how bad it is: hard, degraded, warning or tolerated.
topics.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES
